headline_hook: The Pope Summons AI Safety, DeepMind Ships a Math Agent, and You Can Build a Robot for $2,500
preview_topics: Chris Olah at the papal encyclical

pick_of_the_day.thesis: ClickUp replacing hundreds of employees with thousands of AI agents is the first time a major SaaS company has publicly framed layoffs as an agent-substitution strategy — and the playbook it's writing will be copied by every mid-market software company within 18 months.

model_literacy.relevance: With task-specific small models outperforming frontier generalists by 4-8x, on-policy distillation — where a student model learns from its own outputs corrected by a teacher — is the technique making those speed gains possible. It's why MiniCPM5 can pack multimodal capabilities into 1B parameters.

items.title: Chris Olah Addresses the Vatican on AI Safety — A First for the Industry
items.angle: An AI lab co-founder speaking at a papal encyclical presentation signals that frontier AI safety has reached the highest levels of global moral authority — this isn't a tech conference, it's a civilizational conversation.
items.key_fact: First AI researcher invited to present at a papal encyclical ceremony

items.title: Anthropic Reportedly Closing $30B+ Round at $900B+ Valuation
items.angle: If confirmed, Anthropic becomes the most valuable private AI company — proof that safety-focused labs can compete commercially, not just morally.

items.title: ClickUp Replaces Hundreds of Employees with AI Agents
items.angle: The first major SaaS company to publicly frame mass layoffs as an agent-substitution strategy — the labor-displacement story just went from theoretical to operational.
items.key_fact: Hundreds of employees replaced with thousands of AI agents

items.title: TechCrunch: The Pope's AI Encyclical Isn't Really About AI
items.angle: Read alongside Olah's remarks — the Church sees concentrated power and eroding democracy, the labs see alignment. The gap between these framings is the real story.
items.key_fact: Encyclical titled 'Magnifica humanitas' uses AI as lens for older power-concentration problems

items.title: DeepMind Ships AlphaProof Nexus — Research-Level Math Goes Agentic
items.angle: DeepMind's theorem-proving capabilities are now wrapped in an agentic framework anyone can use — this is the productization of the Erdős-conjecture work, and it makes research-level math a callable tool.
items.key_fact: Agentic framework for research-level mathematical theorem proving

items.title: Anthropic Publishes First Glasswing Progress Report
items.angle: The first public accounting of what Anthropic's frontier AI cybersecurity initiative has actually discovered — moving from early partner learnings to concrete findings.
items.key_fact: First formal progress report on Project Glasswing's cybersecurity findings

items.title: On-Policy Distillation: The Post-Training Technique Everyone Is Using
items.angle: The clearest explanation yet of why on-policy distillation — student learns from its own outputs corrected by a teacher — is becoming the default post-training recipe.
items.key_fact: Outperforms traditional distillation; becoming the default post-training method

items.title: HuggingFace Drops LeRobot — A $2,500 Open-Source Humanoid You Can Build
items.angle: HuggingFace is doing for robotics what it did for NLP — full open-source hardware + software stack at hobbyist pricing. The barrier to entry for humanoid robotics just collapsed.
items.key_fact: $2,500 for a full humanoid robot kit with open-source stack

items.title: 6-Person Team Ships Task-Specific Models 4-8x Faster Than Frontier Labs
items.angle: 500K downloads prove the specialization thesis isn't just benchmarks — small teams building narrow models can genuinely outrun OpenAI and Anthropic on speed for defined tasks.

items.title: LongCat Releases SOTA Talking-Avatar Model Under MIT License
items.angle: The open-source avatar generation space just got another strong contender — developers building video agents now have real options without vendor lock-in.
items.key_fact: MIT licensed, likely state-of-the-art for open talking-avatar generation

items.title: MiniCPM5 Packs Multimodal Into 1B Parameters
items.angle: Small enough to run on phones and edge devices with full multimodal capabilities — the capable-tiny-model trend keeps accelerating.

items.title: Hermes Agent Adds OpenHands Orchestration — Mix Coding Agents in One Workflow
items.angle: The first agent-of-agents tool that lets you orchestrate Claude Code, Codex, and OpenHands together via installable skills — multi-provider agent coordination is now a real workflow.
items.key_fact: First tool to mix coding agents from different providers in a single workflow

items.title: Agent Swarms: One Prompt Routes Tasks to Gemini, Opus, and GPT
items.angle: The 'best model for each subtask' pattern is becoming a real architecture — assign coding to Opus, research to Gemini, testing to GPT, all from a single prompt.
items.key_fact: Multi-model orchestration: Gemini 3.1 Pro, Opus 4.7, GPT 5.5 in one system

items.title: HuggingFace Publishes the Definitive Agent Terminology Glossary
items.angle: Harness vs. scaffold vs. agent vs. tool — as architectures get complex, imprecise terminology causes real engineering bugs. This is the reference to bookmark.
items.key_fact: Definitive glossary distinguishing harness, scaffold, agent, and tool

items.title: How to Let a Sandboxed Coding Agent Test Changes in Your Browser
items.angle: Solves the 'secure but usable' problem — run Claude Code in a remote VM sandbox while still testing UI changes locally via port forwarding.
items.key_fact: Port forwarding from sandboxed remote VM to local browser for agent testing

items.title: Louis Rossmann Open-Sources His Anti-AI-Slop CLAUDE.md
items.angle: A portable CLAUDE.md plus skills that force Claude away from generic AI tone — a practical template for anyone fighting slop in their own writing output.
items.key_fact: Complete CLAUDE.md + skills config for authentic voice, open-sourced on GitHub

items.title: Amazon's Bee AI Wearable: Same Privacy Tension, Different Distribution
items.angle: Same convenience-vs-privacy tension that killed Humane, but Amazon's distribution advantage could be the difference this time.
items.key_fact: Hands-on review of Amazon's new AI wearable device

quick_links.title: Hackers Are Exploiting Chatbot 'Personalities' — A New Attack Surface
quick_links.angle: Adversarial attacks evolving from jailbreaks to exploiting the character layer
quick_links.key_fact: New attack vector targeting behavioral instructions, not model weights

quick_links.title: Even Google Is Making Up AI Security as It Goes
quick_links.angle: If the deepest security bench in tech doesn't have a playbook, neither do you
quick_links.key_fact: TechCrunch analysis of Google's real-time AI security improvisation

quick_links.title: Clawd Easter Egg: Scroll Down in Claude Code Mobile and the Mascot Comes Alive
quick_links.angle: Anthropic investing in developer delight beyond pure functionality
quick_links.key_fact: Hidden animation in Claude Code iPhone app
